captured_note: AIMv2 appears in the capture's Step-3 Autoreg-SSL evaluation (methods_step3/ARSSL) as an as-is comparison (Track A): the official multimodal-autoregressively pretrained backbone is downloaded and a linear probe is fit on its frozen features, because the from-scratch pretraining (billions of image-text pairs, many GPU-days) is not reproduced. This port carries that as-is comparison only. There is NO author submodule: the AIMv2 model class is timm's (a pinned pip dependency, timm==1.0.28), imported not copied, and the weights are a sha256-pinned download.

paper.title: Multimodal Autoregressive Pre-training of Large Vision Encoders

note: Eval-only port (a single linear_eval stage, no pretraining). The backbone is timm's aimv2_large_patch14_224.apple_pt, built with pretrained=False and the sha256-pinned checkpoint (backbone_artifact below) loaded into it. Because the source is a pip dependency and not a git submodule, this file records NO upstream block and the adapter defines no UPSTREAM (test_port_completeness's both-places rule requires them to agree, and here both are absent).
linear_eval: Probes AIMv2's pooled pre-classifier feature (timm model built with num_classes=0), frozen. AIMv2's multimodal autoregressive pretraining is a genuine representation-learning objective, so the number is comparable (the 'pretrained-backbone reuse' row, analogous to eva02 / DINOv2 / Franca). A real run needs the official checkpoint (backbone_artifact below, fetched and hash-verified by bin/fetch-weights.py --artifact backbone_artifact, passed as the config's train.ckpt); the hermetic smoke leaves ckpt empty and builds a random tiny AIMv2, so nothing is downloaded and only the pipeline is exercised. See docs/EVAL_DOWNLOAD.md.

backbone_artifact.name: AIMv2-Large/14 224px backbone (timm)
backbone_artifact.sha256_source: read on 2026-08-27 from the HuggingFace LFS metadata (https://huggingface.co/api/models/timm/aimv2_large_patch14_224.apple_pt, siblings[].lfs.sha256 for pytorch_model.bin at revision 4ecf1a8825bbd2b5a334523c67c428b6b9a34ca1); bin/fetch-weights.py re-verifies this value on download

rewritten_during_the_port: the model class is timm's, not a copied or submoduled author repository; the pretrained weights are a sha256-pinned HuggingFace download (backbone_artifact) rather than a timm pretrained=True auto-download, so CI never fetches and a real run is hash-verified
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA
features are extracted in fp32 (no autocast), so the frozen-feature probe runs identically on a CPU or a pre-Ampere GPU

the probe follows this port's shared frozen-backbone protocol (mean-centre + L2-normalise, a single linear layer with SGD + cosine), returning the four comparable linear-probe accuracies and the epoch count

the input normalisation is taken from the backbone's own timm data config (AIMv2 uses a CLIP-style mean/std, not ImageNet's); the crop resolution is read from the config so the hermetic smoke can shrink it and build a random tiny AIMv2-style VisionTransformer (RMSNorm, SwiGLU MLP, no class token) instead of the full ViT-L/14
